**Area:** [Media](../COVERAGE.md#media) · **Apple:** [AudioToolbox](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/audiotoolbox) · **Issues:** [`area:media`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Amedia)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** isim's own Audio Units, AUGraph and queues on the mixer; codecs through the host's libavcodec.
- **Objective-C / C interface:** `<AudioToolbox/AudioToolbox.h>` (`isim/sdk-src/Frameworks/AudioToolbox`: Apple's header
  set, `AudioComponent.h` … `AudioServices.h`, plus `<MacTypes.h>`) over the same Swift implementation:
  `swift/overlays/AudioToolbox/CAPI.swift` exports each C function (`@_cdecl`), and `AudioToolbox.framework`
  re-exports `libswiftAudioToolbox`, so an `AudioUnit` or `AudioQueueRef` made in C is the object Swift code sees
  (SDL, FMOD, OpenAL and miniaudio use this interface).
  Music Player, Music Device, Audio File Stream and CAClock (`MusicPlayer.h`, `MusicDevice.h`, `AudioFileStream.h`,
  `CAClock.h`, issue #389) are exported by `CAPIMusic.swift` the same way.
